title: Meet Notely, the app we build
summary: Start here: the small notes app every lesson builds on, and its four parts, introduced one at a time.
youWillLearn: The four parts behind almost every app you will build: browser, app server, database and an AI API
Which part does what when Maya clicks a button

glossary.browser: The program Maya uses to open websites, like Chrome or Safari. It shows the screens and sends her clicks on.
glossary.app server: A computer, somewhere else, that runs the app's own code and answers the browser.
glossary.Next.js: A popular toolkit for writing web apps. Notely's code is written with it.
glossary.Vercel: A company that runs your code on its servers, so you do not need your own.
glossary.request: A message from one part to another asking for something: save this note, give me my notes.
glossary.database: A program built to store data safely and find it again fast.
glossary.Supabase: A service that runs a database for you (and adds logins and file storage). Notely keeps its notes there.
glossary.Claude API: Anthropic's AI, reached over the internet: you send it text, it sends text back. Each call costs a little money.

steps.title: This is Notely, and this is Maya
body: In this course we build and improve one small app: Notely. You write notes in it, and a Summarize button turns a long note into three short lines.
Maya is one of its users. We will follow her clicks to meet the parts of the app, one at a time.

callout.text: Every lesson starts from this picture and changes one thing. If a lesson ever loses you, come back here.

scene.caption: Maya, a Notely user. The rest of the app appears one piece at a time.

steps.title: What Maya sees: the browser
body: Maya opens Notely in her browser, the program she uses for every website. It draws Notely's screens and picks up her typing and clicks.
The browser lives on Maya's laptop. It only knows her screen, so it cannot keep notes safe for everyone. It passes her clicks on.
changes: + Browser: the screen Maya types into, on her laptop

scene.caption: Maya uses Notely through her browser.

steps.title: The app server does the work
body: When Maya presses Save, her browser sends a request to the app server: a computer elsewhere that runs Notely's code. It does the work and answers.
Its code is written with Next.js, a toolkit for web apps, and runs on Vercel, a company that runs code for you. Both just mean: our app server.
changes: + App Server: runs Notely's code, on Vercel
+ Blue dot out: Maya's request. Green dot back: the answer

scene.caption: The browser asks, the app server answers.

steps.title: The database remembers
body: The app server forgets everything once it has answered. Notes need a home that remembers: a database, a program built to store data safely and find it again fast.
Notely's database runs on Supabase, a service that runs it for us. Postgres, the name you will see often, is the kind of database inside.
changes: + Database: keeps every note, run by Supabase
~ Maya steps back for a moment

scene.caption: The app server stores and reads notes in the database.

steps.title: The Claude API writes the summary
body: The Summarize button needs an AI. The app server sends the note's text to the Claude API: Anthropic's AI model, reached over the internet. A few seconds later, the summary comes back.
Every call costs a little money, so the app server decides when to call it. The browser never talks to Claude directly.
changes: + Claude API: the AI that writes summaries
~ Database steps back: this step is about the AI

scene.caption: The app server asks the Claude API for a summary.

steps.title: One click, start to finish
body: Maya clicks Summarize. Her browser sends a request to the app server. The server reads the note from the database, sends its text to the Claude API, saves the summary, and answers the browser.
Four parts, one click, about two seconds. Almost every app you will build has this same shape.
changes: ~ Everything is back in view, working together
~ Database: reads the note, then saves the summary

scene.caption: One click touches all four parts.

steps.title: Where the course goes from here
body: Today Notely has one user. In the lessons ahead it grows to thousands, and every part gets a chance to break: data gets messy, keys leak, the AI gets slow or expensive.
Each lesson zooms into one part of this picture, says what goes wrong, and shows the fix.

callout.text: When Claude Code builds an app for you, ask it to name these four parts in your project: which file is the server code, where the database is, and where the Claude API is called.

scene.caption: The same four parts, now serving a crowd.

quiz.question: Maya saves a note today. Where is it kept, so it is still there next month?

options.why: The browser only shows the screens. Clear it, or switch laptops, and anything kept there is gone.
The app server forgets everything once it has answered a request. It hands the note to the database.
That is its job: keep data safely and find it again fast.

quiz.question: Which part talks to the database and to the Claude API?

options.why: It runs Notely's code and holds the keys to both, so they never reach Maya's laptop.
The browser only talks to the app server. Giving it the keys would hand them to every visitor.
Claude only answers what the app server sends it. It does not reach into Notely's database.

takeaways: Notely is the notes app we build all course. Maya is one of its users.
The browser shows the screens. The app server runs the code. The database remembers. The Claude API writes the summaries.
Next.js on Vercel means: our app server. Supabase means: our database.
Only the app server talks to the database and the AI. The browser talks to the app server.
